children: ) today filed their response to Canadian Pacific Kansas City’s request that the Surface Transportation Board (STB) terminate review of the proposed transcontinental railroad, which will be the nation’s first single-line, seamless coast-to-coast railroad.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261119356896/en/

As made clear in their response and an accompanying verified statement from CEO Jim Vena, Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern consistently support a full, transparent and rigorous review of the proposed merger and encourage all stakeholders to make their views known to the STB.

“I have spoken publicly in front of numerous groups before and since the merger announcement. I have also spoken to and with hundreds of our customers. I do use humor in my presentations to keep the audience engaged, including in my presentation at the conference of the Southwest Association of Rail Shippers this past March. I know what I said and regret the inference. The speech was over 50 minutes long, and I made an attempt at humor at the end of that presentation. I apologize to anyone who misunderstood my statement,” said Vena.

Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern remain focused on advancing a transaction that will give U.S. businesses more options to compete in the global marketplace, lower transportation costs and protect tens-of-thousands of union jobs. The companies look forward to the STB's continued evaluation of the proposed combination based on the facts, evidence and public interest benefits presented in the record. For more information, visit AmericasGreatConnection.com.

Norfolk Southern also has the most extensive intermodal network in the eastern U.S. It serves a majority of the country's population and manufacturing base, with connections to every major container port on the Atlantic coast as well as major ports across the Gulf Coast and Great Lakes.
